    def test_port_boundary_and_error_details(self):
        """Regression tests for port boundary values and error specifics.

        Verifies that port validation errors occur when accessing the .port
        attribute, not when constructing the result. Checks the exact
        exception class, args tuple, and message.
        """
        parse_funcs = (urllib.parse.urlsplit, urllib.parse.urlparse)

        # Valid boundary ports: assert concrete return values.
        for parse in parse_funcs:
            # No port at all → None
            p = parse("http://example.com/")
            self.assertIsNone(p.port)
            p = parse(b"http://example.com/")
            self.assertIsNone(p.port)
            # Port 0 (lower bound)
            p = parse("http://example.com:0/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 0)
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:0/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 0)
            # Port 65535 (upper bound)
            p = parse("http://example.com:65535/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 65535)
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:65535/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 65535)

        # Invalid ports: ValueError raised at .port access, not at parse.
        # Each entry is (port_value, expected_message).
        str_invalid = [
            # Empty port: no digits
            ("", "Port could not be cast to integer value as ''"),
            # One above upper bound
            ("65536", "Port out of range 0-65535"),
            # Negative: minus sign makes it not a digit string
            ("-1", "Port could not be cast to integer value as '-1'"),
            # Non-integer: letters
            ("abc", "Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'"),
            # Non-ASCII decimal digit (Devanagari 6)
            ("\u0966", None),
        ]
        bytes_invalid = [
            (b"", "Port could not be cast to integer value as b''"),
            (b"65536", "Port out of range 0-65535"),
            (b"-1", "Port could not be cast to integer value as b'-1'"),
            (b"abc", "Port could not be cast to integer value as b'abc'"),
        ]

        for parse in parse_funcs:
            for port, msg in str_invalid:
                if msg is None:
                    msg = (f"Port could not be cast to integer value "
                           f"as {port!r}")
                url = "http://example.com:" + port + "/"
                p = parse(url)
                self.assertEqual(p.netloc, "example.com:" + port)
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
                    _ = p.port
                self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args, (msg,))
                self.assertEqual(str(ctx.exception), msg)

            for port, msg in bytes_invalid:
                url = b"http://example.com:" + port + b"/"
                p = parse(url)
                self.assertEqual(p.netloc, b"example.com:" + port)
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
                    _ = p.port
                self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.args, (msg,))
                self.assertEqual(str(ctx.exception), msg)
